hero.description: A tightly kept record of deck versions, matchup plans, and format reads for players who want their testing to survive contact with a tournament room.
hero.standardFootnote: Play the room, not the hype.
hero.speaker: Prof. Elm

brief.title: Your field read should have an expiry date.
brief.description: Prize Map keeps the source window, confidence, and next test visible—so a strong result never disguises a stale conclusion.

featured.title: Decks, field reads, and the decisions behind them.

posts.title: Decks, field reads, and the decisions behind them.
posts.description: A searchable archive of versioned reports and source-aware format reads.
posts.emptyState: No notes match that field read. Reset the filters and try another term.

field.title: A format read is a timestamped argument.
field.description: This page is reserved for live, source-backed meta snapshots. The starter workspace deliberately makes no unverified claim about today’s Standard field—competitive information needs a source window before it needs a hot take.

steps.title: Snapshot
steps.description: Record the format, events observed, sample window, and update date.

steps.title: Read
steps.description: Separate results you saw from the decision you infer from them.

steps.title: Action
steps.description: End with the deck, tech, or matchup test the field read changes.

protocol.title: Make a competitive journal that remains useful after the event.
protocol.description: Prize Map is a static, Markdown-authored publishing system for a serious Pokémon Trading Card Game player. It is built to preserve list versions, timestamp metagame observations, and turn testing into advice that can be checked later.

principles.title: Own the source.
principles.description: Posts live as validated Markdown in the repository, not as opaque CMS records.

principles.title: Keep the conditions.
principles.description: Format, date, deck version, and confidence are first-class editorial context.

principles.title: Publish the next decision.
principles.description: The value is what you will test, play, or cut next—not a retrospective victory lap.

notFound.title: That note is not in this deck.
notFound.description: It may have moved, or it has not been published yet.
